title: Sandworm_Exaramel_Backdoor_Investigation_9d8
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sandworm Exaramel backdoor malware. This malware is known for its persistence, C2 communication, and lateral movement capabilities. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.
outcomes: Identify and investigate suspicious services and processes.
Analyze network communication for signs of C2 activity.
Collect and verify evidence of malicious activity.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sandworm Exaramel backdoor malware. This malware is known for its persistence, C2 communication, and lateral movement capabilities. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: investigator, Password: SecurePass123. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: investigator, Password: SecurePass123. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the target host, you notice unusual network activity. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service running on port 4444 is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. Investigate the persistence mechanisms used by the service.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, you can check the systemd service unit files. The systemd service unit file responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service is located at `/etc/systemd/system/bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for systemd service files or cron jobs that might be responsible for starting the service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd service unit files using the command `ls /etc/systemd/system/`.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: Exaramel malware is known for its lateral movement capabilities. Investigate the target host to identify any evidence of file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts.
levels.solution: To investigate lateral movement, you can check the system logs and network connections for any unusual activity involving the next-target host. The service responsible for the lateral movement activity is `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the system logs and network connections for any unusual activity involving the next-target host.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `journalctl -u payload-transfer.service` to check the logs of the payload-transfer service.
